newsitem.title: UK: Coffee crop estimates - Main AFRICAN producers.
newsitem.headline: Coffee crop estimates - Main AFRICAN producers.

text.p: The following table gives latest estimates of 1996/97 coffee crops in main African coffee producing countries (estimates of 1995/96 crops in brackets).
Crop years and approximate main harvesting periods (as supplied by economists) follow each entry (in million 60 kg bags) -
SEE BELOW TABLE FOR MORE DETAILED NOTES ON HARVESTS, CRUCIAL WEATHER PERIODS.

ETHIOPIA - Peak harvest period is October-December. The first flowering is Jan/Feb, second April/May and the third June/July. Beans start developing in March and it takes 23-32 weeks for strong beans to develop. After 32 weeks main cherries develop. Good rains and sunny intervals are required for flowering and up to the development of the main cherries.
IVORY COAST - coffee trees flower mainly in January for cherries harvested 9-11 months later, around October and November.
Abnormally dry weather between December and March or wet weather between March and June, especially towards the end of that period, can damage developing cherries.
Local buyers seek coffee from December with export activity picking up in February and March after peak cocoa marketing.
Ivory Coast's main rainy season (March-June) is followed by a short dry spell (July-August), lighter rains (between September-November) and the main dry season (December-early March).
New plantings take about five years to produce crop.
UGANDA - Harvesting in the key growing areas of central and eastern Uganda runs from October to March.
